messages.content: Now that the Kansas City flights are set, I need a hotel for Monday, January 11 through Thursday, January 14. One room, one adult. Please compare the two properties we discussed by full cost, not just the nightly rate.

I have the Cascade Hotel Kansas City near the museum at $219 per night and the Hampton Inn & Suites Kansas City-Country Club Plaza at $174 per night. I’ll calculate taxes and required fees for all three nights and verify the Tuesday morning trip to the museum along with each cancellation deadline.
Good. I need to be at the Nelson-Atkins staff entrance by 8:15 Tuesday morning. What are the actual totals?

For January 11-14, the Cascade is $657 in room charges, $111.03 in lodging taxes, and a required $25-per-night destination fee plus $12.68 tax on that fee. The complete three-night total is $855.71. The Hampton is $522 in room charges plus $88.22 in lodging taxes, with no destination or resort fee, for a complete total of $610.22.
That is a $245.49 difference, correct? And does the Cascade fee include parking? I will not have a car.

Yes. The Cascade costs $245.49 more for the stay. Its destination fee does not include parking; it covers the fitness center, standard Wi-Fi, two daily bottled waters, and a $15 nightly food-and-beverage credit. Since you will not have a car, no parking charge would apply at either hotel.
Please check the Tuesday route from each one. I do not want a general neighborhood estimate. Use the staff entrance on Oak Street.

From the Cascade’s entrance at West 46th Street and Main Street to the Nelson-Atkins staff entrance on Oak Street, the walking route is 0.8 mile and currently maps at about 17 minutes via Main, Emanuel Cleaver II Boulevard, and Oak. Leaving by 7:50 a.m. allows 25 minutes. From the Hampton on West 46th Street, the route is 1.4 miles; a Tuesday rideshare is estimated at 6-10 minutes, plus pickup time, so a 7:55 a.m. pickup request would be prudent.
The Cascade walk is fine. Before I decide, give me the cancellation wording and deadlines for both rates in Kansas City time.

Cascade: cancellation is permitted without charge until 11:59 p.m. Central on Wednesday, January 6, 2027. A cancellation after that deadline, or a no-show, is charged one night’s room rate plus tax, estimated at $256.01. Hampton: cancellation is permitted without charge until 6:00 p.m. Central on Saturday, January 2, 2027. After that time, the entire stay becomes nonrefundable, currently $610.22.
So the Hampton is much cheaper, but I would be committed nine days before arrival and still need a ride Tuesday. Is the Cascade total payable now or at the hotel?

The Cascade flexible rate requires a card guarantee but no advance payment. The hotel collects $855.71 during the stay, and the quoted destination fee is mandatory. A temporary incidental hold may be added at check-in, but it is not part of the room total.
Reserve the Cascade for all three nights through Thursday checkout. Use the museum travel card ending in 1842 and put the room in Avery Thompson’s name.

The Cascade Hotel Kansas City is confirmed for Avery Thompson, one adult, from Monday, January 11 through Thursday, January 14, 2027, under confirmation CPK-714582. The guaranteed total is $855.71: $657 room, $111.03 room tax, $75 destination fees, and $12.68 tax on those fees. The museum travel card ending in 1842 guarantees the reservation; payment is due at the hotel. Cancellation is free through 11:59 p.m. Central on Wednesday, January 6. For Tuesday’s 8:15 a.m. arrival at the Nelson-Atkins Oak Street staff entrance, the mapped walk is 0.8 mile, approximately 17 minutes, with a suggested departure by 7:50 a.m.
